title: Priority processing for students who can't apply in Australia

sections.heading: Prepare before you travel
sections.text:
To help minimise your time outside Australia and any interruptions to your studies, prepare your application and supporting documents before leaving Australia.

Before you travel:

- check your current visa expiry date and plan to leave Australia before it expires
- contact your education provider to confirm what you still need to do for your studies and get a current Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE)
- discuss travel timing and how to manage your studies while overseas. Your provider may have options for you to study online while you wait for your visa decision
- use the My Health Declarations service to confirm if you need a health check. If you do, obtain a HAP ID and book an appointment with Bupa Medical Visa Services in Australia
- prepare your application and use the Document Checklist Tool to check that your application includes all required information and documents.

sections.heading: Apply from outside Australia
sections.text:
Lodge your complete application through ImmiAccount once you are outside Australia. Check ImmiAccount regularly and respond quickly to requests for further information.

Processing times vary. Do not book your return flights or accommodation in Australia until your new Student visa has been granted.

You will not be able to get a Bridging visa if you lodge your application outside Australia because you are not able to lodge inside Australia.

sections.heading: Providing biometrics
sections.text:
Depending on the country you lodge your Student visa application from, you may need to provide biometric information, such as fingerprints and a photograph of your face.

If you need to provide biometrics, you will automatically receive a request letter in ImmiAccount after you lodge your Student visa application. Follow the instructions in the letter to book an appointment promptly. Appointment locations are limited and should be checked in advance.

Appointment wait times vary between countries. Do not make travel arrangements until you have attended your appointment and provided your biometrics.

For more information, including the countries where biometrics are required, see Biometrics.

sections.heading: Check the rules for family members
sections.text:
If you need to apply for a new Student visa outside Australia, because you do not meet an exemption to apply inside Australia, you cannot include family members in your new application unless you meet a separate family member exemption category. This applies even if your family members are included in your current Student visa.

Check the rules for including family members before making plans.

sections.heading: Priority processing
sections.text:
If you need to lodge your further Student visa application outside Australia because you are not eligible to apply in Australia, you may be eligible for priority processing.

If your application is eligible for priority processing, the Department aims to finalise it within 5 business days, provided all requirements, including biometrics and health requirements have been met.

Complete offshore Student visa applications will be prioritised for students who have maintained satisfactory course progress and met their study requirements.

This applies to students studying a higher education course at a higher education provider who:

- have transferred providers or require more than 12 months to complete compulsory professional or clinical placements as part of their qualification (for example, nursing or medical placements), or
- have transferred between Public higher education providers, or
- have transferred providers and, by the time they apply for a further visa, have studied with their new provider for at least 12 months and can demonstrate course progress.

All students must provide evidence that they will complete their course by the end date on their CoE.

Students who meet one of the circumstances listed above are eligible for priority processing, provided all requirements are met, including biometrics and health.

Priority will be considered based on the circumstances of each student, including the applicant’s study history and any changes to their course or provider. Students that have a history of non-commencement, lengthy deferrals or have shown limited progression in their studies will not be given priority processing. Applications that don’t meet priority considerations will be processed according to standard student visa processing priorities.

Priority processing does not guarantee that your visa will be granted. Each application must meet the visa requirements.

Here are two scenarios that help explain when priority processing does and does not apply:

Linh the nursing student who has changed providers and needs extra time to finish her course.

Linh is in Australia studying nursing at a university. Her current Student (subclass 500) visa will expire in 2 months.

In order to complete her practical placement, Linh changed education provider to one with placements available. She now needs additional time to complete this new placement. Her new university has given her a 16-month extension to finish her studies, including time for her placement. This means she needs a new Student visa to cover the additional 14 months after her current visa expires.

Because she changed education providers she is not eligible to apply in Australia under the course completion exemption. Because she needs more than 12 months to complete her course, she is also not eligible to apply in Australia. This means she must be outside Australia to apply for and be granted a new Student visa.

Linh books a flight overseas with an open return date. Before she leaves Australia, Linh uses the Document Checklist tool, prepares all the documents and evidence needed for her visa application. She also arranges a new health examination in Australia using the MyHealth Declaration Service. That way she can lodge her application quickly.

When Linh gets to her accommodation overseas, she lodges her new Student visa application. She also does some study online and arranges a local biometrics collection while waiting for a visa decision. Because her studies were affected by delays in her clinical placement, her application receives priority processing.

Carlos the diploma student who has changed providers and needs more than 12 months to finish his course.

Carlos is in Australia studying a diploma course at a VET provider in regional Victoria. He did not commence that course and instead moved to Melbourne to study a different diploma course with a new provider. He also deferred his studies for an extended period before starting the new course in Melbourne.

His current Student (subclass 500) visa will expire in 4 months. However, because he changed courses and deferred his studies, he will need an extra year to finish his current studies and needs to apply for a new Student visa.

As he does not meet the course completion exemption, Carlos must be outside Australia to apply for and be granted a new Student visa.

Carlos uses the Document Checklist tool to make sure he has everything ready to submit a complete visa application. He also checks the MyHealth Declaration Service to see if he needs a new health examination.

Carlos books a flight back to his home country over the summer break, and leaves the return date open. When he arrives home, he lodges his new Student visa application. Because he did not commence his original course and had a lengthy deferral before starting his new course, his application does not receive priority processing. His application is processed according to the standard student visa processing priorities.

sections.heading: After you apply
sections.text:
If you lodged your application from outside Australia, because you were not eligible to lodge your application inside Australia, you will need to wait outside Australia for your visa to be granted.

However, if you hold a valid visa, you may travel to Australia while your Student visa application is being processed. You must comply with that visa’s conditions. You will not receive a Bridging visa linked to an application lodged outside Australia.

If you are in Australia when your visa is ready to be granted, we may ask you to leave Australia so processing can continue, so you will need to make sure you check your emails regularly for communication from the Department.

sections.heading: Considering a Visitor visa (subclass 600) in urgent circumstances
sections.text:
If your Student visa will expire before you can complete urgent study requirements, and you can’t apply in Australia, a Visitor visa (subclass 600) may be an option . For example, you may have final exams soon that require you to be physically present in Australia.

If you apply for a Visitor visa in Australia, you will receive a Bridging Visa A while your application is processed. A Bridging Visa A will allow you to continue studying. You must meet the requirements for a Visitor Visa, and a visa is not guaranteed. Once granted, a Visitor visa allows study for up to three months.

Before applying, consider how a Visitor visa could affect your future visa options.

If you are granted a Visitor visa:

- You can still apply for a Temporary Graduate (subclass 485) visa, provided your Student visa expired less than six months ago and you meet the Temporary Graduate visa study requirement.
- You cannot apply for a further Student visa (subclass 500) while in Australia

Seek advice from a registered migration agent or lawyer before applying for a Visitor visa. They can help you understand your options and the potential impact on future visa applications.

sections.heading: You have already finished your course
sections.text:
If you have completed your course and want to study a new course in Australia, different rules apply. You may be eligible for the course progression exemption. This allows some students to apply for another Student visa while in Australia.

Check whether you meet the course progression exemption before making plans to travel overseas.

sections.heading: Introduction
sections.text:
The information on this page is for you if you can’t apply for a further student visa in Australia because:

- you have changed education providers since your current Student visa was granted, or
- you need more than 12 months to finish your course, and your provider has given you more time to finish your course.

If you have changed providers or need more than 12 months to finish your course, you do not meet the course completion exemption to apply in Australia.

You must be outside Australia when you lodge your visa application and when your new visa is granted.

Having to apply from outside Australia does not mean you cannot return to Australia to finish your course. You can still apply for another student visa to complete your studies.

If you need to lodge your further Student visa application outside Australia because you are not eligible to apply in Australia, you may be eligible for priority processing.

If your application is eligible for priority processing, the Department aims to finalise it within 5 business days, provided all requirements, including biometrics and health requirements have been met.

As with any visa application, you must meet the visa requirements, and a new visa is not guaranteed.
